1. Foundations of Proof

The language of analysis, from the ground up — propositions and quantifiers through direct proof, contrapositive, contradiction, strong induction, equivalence relations, and function proofs, following the arc of Hammack’s Book of Proof.

  • Propositions and Truth Tables — Switch the connective and watch the new column fill in while the PPP, QQQ columns stay fixed. Compare the shaded P→QP \to QP→Q column with its contrapositive ¬Q→¬P\lnot Q \to \lnot P¬Q→¬P row by row — identical in all four rows. The converse Q→PQ \to PQ→P, though, splits off in the (T,F)(T, F)(T,F) row.
  • Universal and Existential Quantifiers — A game on the number line: the challenger names xxx, and you answer with the bigger point y=x+1y = x + 1y=x+1 — ∀x ∃y (y>x)\forall x \,\exists y \,(y > x)∀x∃y(y>x). Swap the quantifier order and the same game collapses. The ε\varepsilonε-δ\deltaδ line is exactly this pattern, with δ=ε/2\delta = \varepsilon/2δ=ε/2 answering f(t)=2tf(t) = 2tf(t)=2t.
  • Direct Proof — The sum of two rationals r1=p1q1r_1 = \frac{p_1}{q_1}r1​=q1​p1​​, r2=p2q2r_2 = \frac{p_2}{q_2}r2​=q2​p2​​ on a number line, with the computation p1q2+p2q1q1q2\frac{p_1 q_2 + p_2 q_1}{q_1 q_2}q1​q2​p1​q2​+p2​q1​​ running straight from hypothesis to conclusion — that is a direct proof.
  • Proof by Contrapositive — The n=1..12n = 1..12n=1..12 grid where the n2n^2n2-even rows are exactly the nnn-even rows — where the direct proof of "n2n^2n2 even ⇒\Rightarrow⇒ nnn even" stalls, the contrapositive "odd nnn ⇒\Rightarrow⇒ odd n2n^2n2" opens up through (2k+1)2=2(2k2+2k)+1(2k+1)^2 = 2(2k^2+2k)+1(2k+1)2=2(2k2+2k)+1.
  • Proof by Contradiction — Suppose the primes p1,…,pkp_1, \ldots, p_kp1​,…,pk​ were all there are — the chips show the list, P=p1⋯pkP = p_1 \cdots p_kP=p1​⋯pk​, and N=P+1N = P+1N=P+1. NNN is divisible by no prime on the list (remainder 1) yet has a prime factor, and that factor is off the list — a contradiction. At k=6k = 6k=6, N=30031=59×509N = 30031 = 59 \times 509N=30031=59×509 is composite and the proof still stands, teaching the shape of contradiction (assume ¬P\lnot P¬P → contradiction → PPP).
  • Proof by Cases and Existence Proofs — Moving the point (x,y)(x, y)(x,y) shades its quadrant and unfolds that case's computation of ∣xy∣=∣x∣⋅∣y∣|xy| = |x|\cdot|y|∣xy∣=∣x∣⋅∣y∣ — the four cases (and the axes) cover the whole plane. And from c=22c = \sqrt{2}^{\sqrt{2}}c=2​2​ two branches fork and rejoin at "irrational a,ba, ba,b exist with aba^bab rational" without ever revealing which branch is true — the flavor of non-constructive existence.
  • Counterexamples and If and Only If — Watch a single counterexample demolish a universal claim, tested on four false claims — every prime is odd, 4∣n2⇒4∣n4 \mid n^2 \Rightarrow 4 \mid n4∣n2⇒4∣n, sums of irrationals are irrational, ∣x∣=∣y∣⇒x=y|x| = |y| \Rightarrow x = y∣x∣=∣y∣⇒x=y. Slide nnn and flip the hypothesis and conclusion lights until ¬(∀x P(x))=∃x ¬P(x)\lnot(\forall x\, P(x)) = \exists x\, \lnot P(x)¬(∀xP(x))=∃x¬P(x) feels mechanical. The mirror skill — proving each arrow of P  ⟺  QP \iff QP⟺Q separately — is carried out in the problems.
  • Strong Induction — Draw the factorization tree of n=30n = 30n=30 and strong induction explains itself — the splits drop to much smaller numbers like 151515 and 222, not to n−1=29n - 1 = 29n−1=29. Slide nnn, watch the tree redraw, and follow the induction step that assumes all of P(2),…,P(n−1)P(2), \dots, P(n-1)P(2),…,P(n−1) at once; the weak hypothesis P(n−1)P(n-1)P(n−1) alone can never reach the factors.
  • Equivalence Relations — Congruence modulo nnn as an equivalence relation: the three axioms — reflexive, symmetric, transitive — are brute-force verified on every element, pair, and triple of U={0,…,3n−1}U = \{0, \dots, 3n-1\}U={0,…,3n−1}, and the classes [r]={r,r+n,r+2n}[r] = \{r, r+n, r+2n\}[r]={r,r+n,r+2n} visibly partition the set as nnn slides.
  • Proofs about Composite Functions — Proofs about composite functions, tested on concrete tables: g∘fg \circ fg∘f injective forces fff injective, g∘fg \circ fg∘f surjective forces ggg surjective — and the arrow diagrams show exactly why the converses fail (ggg need not be injective, fff need not be surjective). For bijections, (g∘f)−1=f−1∘g−1(g \circ f)^{-1} = f^{-1} \circ g^{-1}(g∘f)−1=f−1∘g−1 is computed out loud.
